speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a history of a painful, swollen left ankle that resolved on its own, and now you are experiencing increasing pain and swelling in your right knee along with episodes of pain during urination. To help me understand what might be connecting these symptoms, have you noticed any redness or warmth in either joint?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (formerly Reiter's Syndrome). The combination of asymmetric oligoarthritis (knee, ankle), urethritis (pain with urination), and a history of inconsistent condom use with multiple sexual partners is classic for this condition, often triggered by an infection such as Chlamydia trachomatis.
